turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma'am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Come in, Estella. Show this boy the grounds.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will go with Estella, if that is what you wish.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Very well, go with her. And remember, this place holds secrets better left undisturbed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will be careful and not disturb anything.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Be sure to keep your eyes to the ground, Pip. There are things here that are better left unseen and unheard.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will keep my eyes to the ground and be very careful.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Follow Estella, but remember, this place is a world of its own, with its own rules. Observe, but do not question.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will follow Estella and observe carefully.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Remember, Pip, time stands still in this place. Observe and learn, but do not be surprised by what you see.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I understand, Miss Havisham. I will be very careful and watchful.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: And remember, Pip, in this place, the past is never truly past. It haunts us all.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I will remember that, Miss Havisham. I will try not to be startled by anything.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella will show you around, Pip. Observe her closely, for she is a product of this twisted world.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will pay close attention to Estella and do as you say.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Pay attention to her mannerisms, her coldness. She is a mirror of my own heart, now.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will observe Estella carefully and learn from her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Remember, Pip, the world may be kind to you, but I have learned that it is not kind to everyone. Observe and learn, but do not become like them.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I understand, Miss Havisham. I will remember your words and be careful not to become like the world.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Observe the world, Pip, but do not be of it. Keep your heart locked away, as I have done, or it will be broken again and again.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
